flow.costPlain: What Home Depot paid suppliers for the merchandise it sold, plus the cost of getting it into stores.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Store payroll, rent, advertising and running the head office.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of stores, warehouses and equipment over their useful lives — including $178M of amortization tied to acquired companies like SRS.

follow100Note: Two-thirds of every $100 goes straight back out as the cost of the merchandise itself — retail keeps a much thinner slice than software does. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
oneTimers: Adjusted results exclude $178M of amortization from acquired intangibles (including $125M tied to SRS) — on that basis EPS was $4.92 instead of the GAAP $4.79.
The reaffirmed guidance assumes IEEPA tariff refunds will partly offset unplanned fuel, energy and other product input costs this year.
otherDetail: Interest and other, net was a $524M cost: $583M of interest expense on Home Depot's debt, partly offset by $59M of interest and other income.

segments.name: Net sales
segments.note: Everything sold through 2,364 Home Depot stores and its website, plus the SRS and GMS professional-supply businesses Home Depot has been buying to win more contractor spending.

takeaways.text: Comparable sales rose 1.7% overall and 1.3% in the U.S. Transactions fell 1.0% while the average ticket rose 2.8% to $92.50 — fewer trips, slightly bigger baskets, and a tilt toward smaller projects.
takeaways.title: Same-store growth is barely positive

takeaways.text: Total sales grew 5.7% — far faster than comparable sales. The gap is SRS Distribution and GMS, the professional-supply distributors Home Depot bought so its growth depends less on DIY shoppers waiting out high mortgage rates.
takeaways.title: Acquisitions are doing the heavy lifting

takeaways.text: Home Depot reaffirmed its FY26 plan: sales growth of 2.5–4.5%, comparable sales flat to +2%, and a full-year operating margin around 12.4–12.6%. Management is planning for another year of muted big-project demand.
takeaways.title: Guidance assumes the housing freeze lasts

verdict: Home Depot grew sales 5.7% to $47.9B, but comparable sales rose only 1.7% — shoppers came less often and spent a little more per trip, leaning into smaller projects while big remodels stayed on hold.
